$comment: A theme bundles everything that decides how the terminal LOOKS:
the Windows Terminal colour scheme, the profile defaults that go with it
(opacity, cursor, ...) and the matching PSReadLine syntax colours.
Add a theme by dropping another .json in this folder - the file name is the
theme name, and bootstrap.ps1 -Apply offers every file it finds. Pick one
The chosen name is remembered in ~/.config/pwsh/theme.txt, so later runs of
psreadline values are PSReadLine colour names. A bare '#rrggbb' there sets
Selection and ListPredictionSelected set ONLY a background (\u001b[48;2;R;G;Bm).
Adding a foreground there would repaint selected text a single flat colour,
which no longer matches Windows Terminal's mouse selection - that keeps the
syntax colours and only swaps the background. Keyboard and mouse selection
should look identical, so keep selectionBackground and this value in sync.
description: Tokyo Night - navy dark, muted pastels, 85% opacity
